items.title: Tom Varner interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, August 13, 2025
items.q: So that was a group of Seattle musicians plus the great trumpet player Russ Johnson who is now in the Milwaukee area.

ctx.x: I want to hone in a little bit – when you were talking about your sabbatical and being on the East Coast, the shorter compositions, was this made into “Heaven and Hell”?

That was a little earlier. “Heaven and Hell” was from when I moved to – well I moved – so I’ll make it really quick. All those various things I was doing, that was in New York, go to Europe, back and forth, go blah-blah-blah. Then I got married, then I had kids, then I had two kids. And trying to get the two kids on the subway etcetera, etcetera. My wife was a Seattle native. I’d been in Manhattan for 24, 25 years and so we were like okay, and I had friends that had moved to Seattle, let’s make that move. It’ll…

some of them were much more longer, thought out, composed. I was very fortunate in that a couple years earlier I was able to go to have a residency at the McDowell Colony. Oh that was heaven. Just wonderful. And a lot of the music for “Heaven and Hell” I wrote for that type of configuration. I had to adjust the instrumentation a bit. So but that was a mix of notated compositions with improv and then short takes that were really just like little 60-second meditations kind of. So later, now fast forward to another…
